text.p: A hearing to consider Texaco Inc.'s proposal to settle a racial discrimination suit for $176.1 million been delayed until March 18, a plaintiffs' lawyer said Thursday.
The original date for the hearing had been set for Feb. 27.

Daniel Berger of law firm Bernstein Litowitz Berger & Grossman said that notices to more than 1,300 prospective plaintiffs are expected to be sent on Friday and class members will have until March 4 to decide whether to opt out of the settlement.
Class members are African-Americans who were salaried employees of Texaco between March 23, 1991 and Nov. 15, 1996.
The lawsuit, filed by six Texaco employees in 1994, alleged the company denied promotions and raises to blacks.

Texaco agreed to settle the suit after the release of transcripts of secretly taped conversations that appeared to show white Texaco executives discussing the destruction of documents sought by plaintiffs in the suit.
Texaco also announced it fired a top executive of an insurance unit and had taken actions against other current and former employees who can be heard on the tapes.
